title: Intraday 0DTE Option Order Flow and S&P 500 Downside Risk
one_line: On 1,027 days (May 2022-Jun 2026), a put-heavy gamma-weighted 0DTE put-call ratio at the open predicts weaker next-hour S&P returns and a higher chance of a down hour, but not the DEPTH of declines (vanishes in severe sell-offs), and out of sample a trading rule on it earns nothing significant before or after costs.

findings.statement: Put-heavy opening gamma-weighted PCR → weaker next-hour return, higher P(negative hour).
Link to downside depth fades as declines get larger; absent in severe sell-offs.
Out-of-sample trading rule / probability forecast: no significant profit, no gain over baselines.

why.pattern: Opening 0DTE flow reflects short-term sentiment/hedging demand.

reported_results.headline: On 1,027 days (May 2022-Jun 2026), a put-heavy gamma-weighted 0DTE put-call ratio at the open predicts weaker next-hour S&P returns and a higher chance of a down hour, but not the DEPTH of declines (vanishes in severe sell-offs), and out of sample a trading rule on it earns nothing significant before or after costs.

tradable_edge: No strategy: negative out-of-sample result and needs 0DTE order-flow data we do not have. Useful as evidence that options-flow signals are a risk filter at best.
